lines: Meet MeetingScribe.
It turns your Teams, Zoom and Google Meet calls into clean notes, and sends them where your team works.
Without anything leaving your computer, unless you say so.
Meetings create work.
But notes go unwritten, action items get lost, and the tickets never get raised.
MeetingScribe runs quietly in the background.
When you join a call, it starts recording two tracks: your microphone, and the meeting's own audio.
No buttons to press, and no bot joining the meeting.
When the call ends, everything runs right on your computer.
Whisper transcribes both tracks.
A voice model tells the speakers apart, and names only the people it is sure about.
A local language model drops the small talk, then writes the summary and the action items.
When it finishes, a Markdown note lands in your Meeting Notes folder, and in the app.
Who was there, who did the talking, what was decided, and who owes what.
And real meetings do not always stay in one language.
If the conversation moves from English to Hindi and back again, it keeps up, and writes each part down in its own script.
An unknown voice? Hear a clip, and name it once.
From then on, it is recognised, as long as there is evidence that person attended.
A stand-up is not a one-on-one, and an incident review is not a customer call.
So each kind of meeting gets the sections it needs, picked from the words in its title.
And if your team has its own way of doing things, you can add your own.
Then there is the part that usually gets lost: who said they would do what.
Every action item from every meeting lands on one list, and work that keeps coming back shows up as carried over.
Tick one off here, and it is ticked in the note too.
Before your next call, it reminds you where you left off.
What was said last time, and what is still open.
It comes straight from your own notes, with no AI involved, so nothing is made up.
Then, connectors put the meeting to work in whatever your team already uses.
Slack, Teams, Gmail and Outlook. Jira. Or an AI that takes on the work. Use the ones you have, and ignore the rest.
Send the recap to a Slack or Teams channel, or open it as a draft in Gmail or Outlook.
Everyone who took something on can get a follow-up with only their work.
You can edit every message, and each one goes only when you press its button.
And action items do not have to wait for you.
Choose Hand to AI on any one. Your local or company AI reads the task, works out where it belongs, and asks what it needs to know.
You answer, and choose where it works: one repository, several, or a plain folder.
And if you already work with an AI assistant, it can read your meetings too.
Turn it on, and Claude or Cursor on your computer can look up what was decided, and what is still open.
It can only read, and it stays off until you say otherwise.
One thing matters more than all of this. There is no bot in the call, so nobody can see that MeetingScribe is there.
Telling people is up to you, so it gives you a notice to paste into the chat.
You can also list the meetings it must never record, and have old ones deleted automatically.
By default, recording, transcription, and every model stay on your computer.
The only things that leave are the messages and Jira updates you approve, sent where you chose.
Before you rely on it, here is the honest part. Read every note before you act on it, because the AI can get details wrong.
It also asks a lot of your computer. Without a fast graphics card or an Apple chip, processing can take longer than the meeting.
The installers are not signed yet, so your computer will warn you when you open them.
It is still early. It has been tested mostly on simulated calls, and the calendar, Slack and Teams only against stand-ins.
And recording people comes with rules. Tell them, and follow the law and your company's policy.
Install it once, join your meetings as usual, and read the notes when you are ready.
MeetingScribe. Meetings, written down, and followed up.
